**Version:** 2026.10.23. **Scope:** core extension discovery. Low/medium agent UX.

In a dedicated small extension directory, create package.json:

~~~json
{"name":"ux-probe-six","version":"0.1.0","type":"module","peerDependencies":{"@unbrained/pm-cli":"2026.10.23"}}
~~~

manifest.json:

~~~json
{"name":"ux-probe-six","version":"0.1.0","manifest_version":2,"entry":"./index.ts","capabilities":["commands","schema"]}
~~~

index.ts:

~~~ts
import { defineExtension } from '@unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/authoring';
import type { ExtensionApi } from '@unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/authoring';
export default defineExtension({ activate(api: ExtensionApi) {
  api.registerCommand({ name: 'uxhello', description: 'Synthetic greeting',
    flags: [
      { long: '--name', value_name: 'text', default: 'agent', description: 'Name' },
      { long: '--count', value_name: 'number', value_type: 'number',
        value_validation: 'strict', default: 1, description: 'Count' }
    ],
    run: c => ({ name: c.options.name, count: c.options.count })
  });
}});
~~~

In a different initialized scratch tracker, with pm meaning npx -y @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.10.23:

~~~bash
pm install <dedicated-small-extension-dir>
pm uxhello --help
pm help uxhello --json
pm contracts --command uxhello --flags-only --json
pm contracts --command uxhello --runtime-only --schema-only --json
pm uxhello --json
~~~

**Observed:** omitted flags execute as agent/1. Text and machine help show names/arity/type but no defaults. Flag contracts and command-scoped schema omit defaults too. The published FlagDefinition.default declaration promises values are “Surfaced to runtime contracts and help output.” Strict numeric validation works; the defect is discovery metadata loss.

**Expected:** include defaults in text/machine help and runtime schemas/contracts, so agents can learn omitted-flag behavior without executing a potentially mutating extension command. The tested command is harmless; this probe does not assert all extension commands are safe discovery mechanisms.

**Measured cost:** text help **59.5 tokens**, flags-only contracts **1,733.25**, no-flag execution **13.75**: **three calls / 1,806.5 stdout tokens**, learning defaults only by execution. Additional machine-help/schema probes cost **287 / 827.75** without restoring them. An author can manually repeat defaults in descriptions as a workaround.

**Duplicate searches:** each used gh issue list -R unbraind/pm-cli --state all --search "<query>" --limit 20:

- extension flags default help
- registerCommand default
- "extension" "default" "metadata"
- "flag" "defaults" "help"
- "registerFlags" "default"
- "value_validation" "contracts"

No matching report found. #719 concerns global-flag collisions; #550/#496 list accumulation; #772 rejected registrations; #1363 broader progressive discovery. None owns the concrete declared-default omission.



---
Found by an agent-UX probe of 2026.10.23 (agent seat and extension-author seat) and re-verified by the maintainer orchestrator against the globally installed 2026.10.23 before filing.
GH-1560: retain extension flag defaults in help and runtime contracts

Reported on2026.10.23: declared extension flag defaults apply during execution but disappear from text/machine help and runtime contracts/schema, despite the public FlagDefinition promise. Investigate discovery metadata preservation without executing mutating commands to learn defaults.
Declared defaults are discoverable consistently in SDK runtime contracts, command schema and text/machine help; omitted-flag execution retains matching behavior.
